_comment: Safety baseline for autonomous Conductor runs in this work_dir. The Conductor opens SDK sessions with settingSources:['project'] and cwd=this directory, so the baseline in claude_code/DEV/full_stack_sm/.claude/settings.json is never seen from here. Without this file, runs had no deny list and no PreToolUse guard at all. CORRECTION (2026-08-26): this comment used to claim settings.local.json is loaded too, and the 'allow' rules were parked there on that assumption. It is NOT — settingSources:['project'] loads THIS file only; 'local' is a separate source the Conductor does not pass. So every allow rule in settings.local.json has been invisible to autonomous runs, and with permissionMode 'acceptEdits' only edits are auto-approved: Bash/WebSearch/WebFetch fell through to a permission prompt that a headless run cannot answer, i.e. a silent deny. That is why the ai-tells detector never ran on the 2026-08-25 article (blocked twice, in seo-editor Pass 3c and again in seo-publisher, and reported as a 'sandbox restriction') and why the shipped draft cites zero third-party sources. The allow list below is the autonomous-run set and must live HERE. Still deliberately no 'ask' array — a headless session cannot answer a prompt; irreversible actions are gated by the Conductor's ASK_PATTERNS over Telegram and by hooks/guard.py.

permissions._allow_comment: Scoped to what the pipelines actually shell out for: the ai-tells detector (referenced by seo-editor, social-editor, message-sequencer, brand-checker and the page-builder skill), the outbound registry, and the Ahrefs keyword pull that feeds seo-planner's keywords_raw. Deliberately NOT the broad 'Bash(python3:*)' that settings.local.json carries for interactive use: guard.py can only pattern-match a command STRING, so `python3 -c "..."` would sail past every rule in it. Narrow script rules keep arbitrary python out of autonomous runs while letting the reviewed scripts through. Both bare and ./-prefixed forms are listed because a blocked path variant fails the same silent way this fix exists to stop. WebSearch/WebFetch are needed for the writer's source-fetching; fetches are read-only and the deny list still blocks secret reads.
